translation_edits.from: But Yahweh is the true God[a]; he is the living God and the everlasting King. At his wrath the earth quakes[c][b], and the nations cannot endure his indignation.
translation_edits.to: But Yahweh[a] is the true God[b]; he is the living God and the everlasting King[c]. At his wrath the earth quakes, and the nations cannot endure his indignation.[d]
translation_edits.rationale: a addresses the conjunction/name phrase; b is the alternative God of truth; c is eternal King. None concerns quaking. d addresses inclusion of the whole verse.

translation_edits.from: Hebrew: 'And the LORD'; the conjunction may also be read simply as connective, but here it likely carries a contrast with the idols described in the surrounding context.
translation_edits.to: Hebrew: 'And Yahweh'; the conjunction may also be read simply as connective, but here it likely carries a contrast with the idols described in the surrounding context.
translation_edits.rationale: The same Hebrew name occurs in the connective alternative and the main rendering. Current DOCTRINE.md renders it Yahweh; changing the conjunction alternative does not replace the name with a title.

value.text: The shorter Greek text represented by Codex Vaticanus lacks verses 6–8 and 10 and places the material of verse 9 within verse 5. A published reconstruction of the fragmentary Hebrew manuscript 4Q71 supports this arrangement. Another ancient Hebrew manuscript, 4Q70, preserves part of verse 10; a form of this verse also appears in the margin of the Greek manuscript Codex Marchalianus. This translation retains the longer Hebrew form; which form is earlier remains unsettled.

from.rationale: Rendered the divine name as 'the LORD' per doctrine default for יְהוָה. The prefixed conjunction can be simply connective ('and') or mildly adversative in context; here 'But' best reflects the contrast with the idols in the preceding context.

to.rationale: The divine name יהוה is rendered 'Yahweh' under current POB policy. The prefixed conjunction can be simply connective ('and') or mildly adversative in context; here 'But' reflects the contrast with the idols in the preceding context.

metadata_edits.rationale: Sync the chosen name with actual text and current doctrine; keep the live conjunction alternative and remove the redundant alternative that is now chosen. HALOT citation retained as historical provenance, not newly consulted evidence.

from.rationale: The immediate literary context contrasts YHWH with idols; rendering the conjunction adversatively preserves that theological and rhetorical contrast without adding content beyond the discourse flow.

to.rationale: The immediate literary context contrasts Yahweh with idols; 'But Yahweh' expresses that contrast, while 'And Yahweh' preserves the connective alternative noted in footnote a.

metadata_edits.rationale: Both documented conjunction alternatives must use the actual current name policy; clarify their note link without changing the main connective interpretation.

required_questions.question: What does the source explicitly say?
required_questions.answer: The fixed WLC opens וַיהוָה, conjunction plus the divine name; אֱלֹהִים אֱמֶת underlies true God/God of truth, and וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם underlies everlasting/eternal King. These source phrases identify the three note locations. The source then continues to quaking earth and the nations' inability to endure divine indignation; the b/c alternatives do not explain those phrases.

required_questions.question: What has English grammar forced us to supply?
required_questions.answer: No new English words are supplied by this package. The existing English copulas and clause links remain unchanged; its adversative But is a contextual choice, not a claim that the Hebrew conjunction only means but. Note a preserves And.

required_questions.question: What interpretation did we keep out of the main text?
required_questions.answer: The connective alternative, God of truth and eternal King remain notes; the shorter literary form and uncertain priority are disclosed only in d. No reconstructed Hebrew, chronological ranking or explanatory material is inserted in main prose.

required_questions.question: Is every uncommon English word necessary for accuracy or register?
required_questions.answer: No uncommon main-text word is introduced. Existing wrath and indignation preserve the already chosen solemn register but are not independently re-adjudicated here. Note d's manuscript names trade some length for exact witness identity.

required_questions.question: Does the verse read naturally aloud in its chapter?
required_questions.answer: Read against 10:3–13, the retained verse supplies Yahweh-focused contrast within idol polemic and intelligible parallel clauses. Anchor movement leaves that prose unchanged. This is a local contextual assessment, not an audio test or complete chapter/book audit.

required_questions.question: Are material differences from major translations or consensus source-justified?
required_questions.answer: No new modern-English comparison panel was consulted and no consensus-based accuracy claim is made. The main English is unchanged. The substantial shorter-form difference is specifically sourced to the prior Swete/DJD dossier, with WLC retained and priority held.
